# Mobile: adb, Logcat & Xcode Simulator

Mobile bugs need evidence from the device itself: which build was installed, what the system log said when the app crashed, which deep link was opened, which permission was denied. On Android the tools are **adb** (Android Debug Bridge) and **Logcat** in Android Studio. On iOS they are the **Xcode Simulator**, its command-line twin **simctl**, and the macOS **Console** app for real devices. This chapter gives the exact setup steps and the commands testers use every day.

| Key fact | Android | iOS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Install** | Android Studio, or only the SDK *platform-tools* (contains `adb`) | Xcode from the Mac App Store (macOS only) |
| **Real device** | USB or Wi-Fi debugging via Developer options | Connect to a Mac. Logs in the **Console** app |
| **Logs** | Logcat (Android Studio) or `adb logcat` | Console app, `xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream` |
| **Emulator / simulator** | Android Emulator (AVD Manager) | Simulator (Xcode → Open Developer Tool → Simulator) |

```diagram
Identify the target (adb devices / simctl list) → clean state (pm clear / erase) → install the exact build → start log capture + screen recording → reproduce (deep link, push, location) → stop and pull files → attach: build number, device, OS version, steps, video, log excerpt
```

## Connecting an Android device: Developer options, USB and wireless debugging

1. On the phone, open **Settings → About phone** and tap **Build number** seven times until you see *You are now a developer*. On some vendors this is under **Software information**.
2. Open **Settings → System → Developer options** and turn on **USB debugging**.
3. Connect the phone by USB and accept the **Allow USB debugging?** prompt with the computer's RSA key fingerprint. Tick **Always allow from this computer** on your own test machine.
4. On the computer run `adb devices -l`. The device must show the state `device`. `unauthorized` means the prompt wasn't accepted, and `offline` means you should reconnect the cable.
5. **Wireless (Android 11+):** in Developer options turn on **Wireless debugging** → **Pair device with pairing code**, then run `adb pair IP:PORT` with the code shown, and finally `adb connect IP:PORT`. The phone and computer must be on the same network.

![Wireless debugging settings on an Android phone](https://developer.android.com/static/studio/images/run/adb_wifi-wireless_debugging_setting.png "Official Android Developers screenshot: the Wireless debugging system setting on a Google Pixel phone.")

```bash
adb devices -l                         # list targets with model and transport
adb -s emulator-5554 shell getprop ro.build.version.release   # Android version of one target
export ANDROID_SERIAL=R58M12345XY      # make one device the default for this terminal
```

> **Caveat:** With more than one device or emulator attached, adb fails with *more than one device/emulator*. Use `-s SERIAL`, `-d` (only USB device) or `-e` (only emulator).

## adb commands QA uses daily: install, deep links, app data, screenshots, video

```bash
# Install / update / remove builds
adb install app-release.apk               # fresh install
adb install -r app-release.apk            # reinstall, keep data (upgrade test)
adb uninstall com.example.shop            # remove app and data

# Clean state without reinstalling
adb shell pm clear com.example.shop       # wipes app data and cache (like first launch)
adb shell am force-stop com.example.shop  # kill the app

# Open screens directly
adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "shop://orders/42"
adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "https://shop.example.com/promo"   # app link

# Permissions
adb shell pm grant  com.example.shop android.permission.CAMERA
adb shell pm revoke com.example.shop android.permission.ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION

# Evidence
adb exec-out screencap -p > screen.png                          # screenshot straight to your PC
adb shell screenrecord --time-limit 60 /sdcard/bug.mp4          # Ctrl+C to stop earlier
adb pull /sdcard/bug.mp4 .
adb bugreport bugreport.zip                                     # full system report for developers

# Device information for the bug report
adb shell getprop ro.product.model
adb shell dumpsys package com.example.shop | grep versionName
```

> **QA tip:** `pm clear` plus a deep link reproduces "first launch from a marketing link" in seconds, which is a scenario that's slow to set up by hand. Text input for long fields is `adb shell input text "hello%sworld"` (`%s` is a space).

## Logcat in Android Studio: filters, crashes and saved queries

1. Run the app on the device or emulator, then open **View → Tool Windows → Logcat**.
2. Choose the device in the dropdown at the top of the Logcat window.
3. Type a query in the filter field. Press `Ctrl+Space` to see suggestions.
4. Start with `package:mine`, which means all packages of the open project. Then narrow it down:

```text
package:mine level:ERROR
package:mine is:crash
package:mine (tag:OkHttp | tag:Retrofit)
package:com.example.shop -tag:Choreographer
package:mine message:"timeout" age:5m
```

| Query | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `level:WARN` | That level and higher (VERBOSE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, ASSERT) |
| `is:crash` | Application crashes, Java or native |
| `is:stacktrace` | Anything that looks like a stack trace |
| `tag:` / `-tag:` | Include or exclude a tag |
| `tag~:Net.*` | Regular expression match |
| `age:5m` | Only the last 5 minutes |

- Click the star next to a query to save it as a favourite. Use **Split Panels** (right-click the log) to watch two queries or devices side by side.
- When the app process restarts after a crash, Logcat prints that the process ended and started again. The lines just before that are the crash.

![The Logcat window in Android Studio](https://developer.android.com/static/studio/images/debug/logcat-window.png "Official Android Developers screenshot: the Logcat window formats logs by time, tag, level and message.")

Without Android Studio, use the command line:

```bash
adb logcat -c                              # clear old logs first
adb logcat -v time > logcat.txt            # save everything with timestamps
adb logcat '*:E'                           # errors and above only
adb logcat -b crash                        # crash buffer only
adb logcat --pid=$(adb shell pidof -s com.example.shop)   # only the running app
```

## Xcode Simulator: devices, screenshots, location and appearance

1. Open **Xcode → Open Developer Tool → Simulator**. Choose a device in **File → Open Simulator** (for example an older, smaller iPhone and the newest one).
2. Install a test build by dragging the `.app` bundle onto the Simulator window, or run it from Xcode.
3. Screenshots: **File → Save Screen** (`Cmd+S`). Video: **File → Record Screen**.
4. Location: **Features → Location** → pick a preset such as **City Run**, or choose **Custom Location…** and enter coordinates.
5. Appearance and accessibility: **Features → Toggle Appearance** (light/dark). Larger text is in the Simulator's Settings app → **Accessibility → Display & Text Size**.
6. Device actions: **Device → Rotate Left / Right**, **Device → Shake**, **Device → Home**, and **I/O → Keyboard → Toggle Software Keyboard**.
7. Reset when you need a clean device: **Device → Erase All Content and Settings…**.

> **Caveat:** The Simulator runs on your Mac's hardware and doesn't fully reproduce real-device behaviour: push notification delivery through APNs, camera, Bluetooth, real performance and memory pressure. Confirm device-specific bugs on a physical iPhone.

## simctl from the terminal: deep links, push, permissions, status bar

`xcrun simctl` controls simulators from scripts. `booted` means "the simulator that is currently running".

```bash
xcrun simctl list devices                                  # all simulators and their UDIDs
xcrun simctl boot "iPhone 16"                              # start a simulator by name
xcrun simctl install booted Shop.app
xcrun simctl launch booted com.example.shop

xcrun simctl openurl booted "shop://orders/42"             # deep link / universal link
xcrun simctl push booted com.example.shop push.json        # local push payload (no APNs)
xcrun simctl location booted set 50.4501,30.5234           # Kyiv
xcrun simctl privacy booted grant photos com.example.shop  # or revoke / reset
xcrun simctl status_bar booted override --time 9:41 --batteryLevel 100 --cellularBars 4
xcrun simctl io booted screenshot shot.png
xcrun simctl io booted recordVideo bug.mp4                 # Ctrl+C to stop
xcrun simctl keychain booted add-root-cert charles-root.pem   # trust a proxy certificate
xcrun simctl erase all                                     # factory-reset all (shut down) simulators
```

An example `push.json` for testing notification handling:

```json
{
  "aps": { "alert": { "title": "Order shipped", "body": "Order #42 is on its way" }, "badge": 1 },
  "orderId": 42
}
```

> **QA tip:** `status_bar override` gives clean, identical screenshots for visual comparisons and store listings. Clear it with `xcrun simctl status_bar booted clear`.

## iOS logs: Console on macOS and simulator log stream

**Real iPhone or iPad**

1. Connect the device to the Mac and trust the computer on the device.
2. Open the **Console** app on the Mac and select the device under **Devices** in the sidebar.
3. Click **Start** to stream messages. Use the search field to filter by process (your app's name) or by text, and **Action → Include Info Messages / Include Debug Messages** if you need more detail.
4. Reproduce the bug, note the exact time, and look for errors and faults around that moment.
5. Crash reports are in Xcode's **Window → Devices and Simulators** for the selected device, and in **Settings → Privacy & Security → Analytics & Improvements → Analytics Data** on the device itself.

**Simulator**

```bash
xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --level debug \
  --predicate 'process == "Shop"'
```

## Cheat sheet

| Task | Command or action |
| --- | --- |
| List Android targets | `adb devices -l` |
| Install / upgrade a build | `adb install -r app.apk` |
| Reset app to first launch | `adb shell pm clear PACKAGE` |
| Open a deep link (Android) | `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "URI"` |
| Screenshot / video (Android) | `adb exec-out screencap -p > s.png` / `adb shell screenrecord` |
| Only your app's errors | Logcat: `package:mine level:ERROR` |
| Crashes | Logcat: `is:crash`, CLI: `adb logcat -b crash` |
| Full report | `adb bugreport bugreport.zip` |
| Open a deep link (iOS Simulator) | `xcrun simctl openurl booted "URI"` |
| Fake push (iOS Simulator) | `xcrun simctl push booted BUNDLE_ID push.json` |
| Fake location | Simulator → Features → Location, or `simctl location` |
| Real iPhone logs | Console app → device → Start |

## Summary

- Identify the exact device or simulator first (`adb devices -l`, `simctl list`). Most "wrong device" mistakes start there.
- `pm clear` / `erase`, deep links, permission grants and fake locations or pushes let you reach any app state quickly and reproducibly.
- Logcat queries such as `package:mine level:ERROR` and `is:crash` turn a wall of logs into evidence. On iOS, use the Console app or `log stream`.
- Attach the build number, device, OS version, steps, a screen recording and a focused log excerpt to every mobile bug report.
